title: I made a short film where an AI assistant drove Unreal and Blender through typed tool calls, with no generative AI in any frame
author: Mifsopo_
selftext:
A rainy alley, a three-letter tag, and a run: [MIF: a graffiti short](https://youtu.be/b_bQOfeKh4k)



Disclosure first: MifBridge is my own plugin, and this film is the showcase for its 1.2 release.



How it was made:



\- An AI assistant (Claude, through MCP) drove Unreal Engine 5.8 and Blender through MifBridge's typed calls: it built the alley, set up the lighting and rain, painted the tag stroke by stroke, cut it in Sequencer, and rendered it.

\- The models were built in Blender the same way, then sent to Unreal.

\- The motion was captured on a phone and solved with MetaHuman Animator.

\- No generative AI anywhere: no generated textures, meshes, images, motion or frames. Every model, material and sound can be opened and changed by hand, because the AI only drove the editors' own tools.



The point of the plugin is that every change is read back from the editor, so the assistant sees what actually happened rather than what it hoped happened. When a value is refused, it gets told which values would work. A person sets the permission level (read, scratch or full) in the editor, and the AI cannot raise it.



1.2 has 717 Unreal commands and 364 Blender operations, on Unreal 5.3 to 5.8 and Blender 3.6 to 5.2. New in this release: gameplay and AI (StateTrees, EQS, GAS), multiplayer testing in play-in-editor, Movie Render Graphs, and in Blender, garments, sculpting, and a game-ready pass that sends a whole kit to Unreal.



Happy to answer questions about the pipeline, what worked, and what the AI was bad at.



More: [https://mifshowcase.store/mifbridge](https://mifshowcase.store/mifbridge)
